title: interop capacity storyboard — weekly walkthrough and sprint handoff
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, annotated storyboard from today’s cross-team sync (infra / SRE / serving runtime) to capture the narrative we want to hand off to the next sprint: how we will reason about regional capacity for the next two marketing-driven demand waves, the priming experiments we’ll run, and the immediate ops playbook for unexpected preemptions.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Agreed approach: two-tier priming + hedged slot buckets per region.
- Short term (this week): roll priming micro-windows in SFO and SIN, increase burst reserve in EU-West by 10%, enable KV-cache warmup in canary serving pool.
- Risk: APAC preemption sensitivity higher; contingency is to shift noncritical serving to cold-backfill region.
- Action items assigned with owners and rough ETA below.

Meeting notes (2026-09-02 10:00–11:05 PT)
Attendees: Aisha (infra), Jon (SRE), Marta (serving runtime), Diego (platform eng), Samira (release eng)
Notes:
- Context: product marketing announced two regional feature rollouts (EU, APAC) with expected 35–60% query uplift during campaign windows. We need to ensure latency SLOs while minimizing committed cost.
- Proposal reviewed: create three slot buckets per region — baseline (reserved), burst (reserved but preemptible), opportunistic (spot/backfill). The novelty: apply short priming micro-windows to warm batch-KV and prefix caches before the predicted peak and keep a small rolling warm pool.
- Marta: serving runtime will expose a simple API flag to trigger prewarm for a model shard; includes a lightweight checksum to ensure KV-cache version matching. She estimates a canary rollout on Tue.
- Jon: SRE will add observability probes for priming success (cache-hit %, cold-start tail p95/p99) and synthetic traffic generators scoped to 10% of expected peak.
- Diego: platform will auto-scale reserve slots using a new heuristic that uses short-term forecast + hedging multiplier; simple config toggle to start with 1.1x for APAC.
- Samira: release engineering calls out deploy freeze windows around 09/10—09/12; we should ensure priming changes land before 09/09.

Operational decisions:
- Short priming windows: run 10m priming 30m before predicted surge for high-risk regions (APAC). For predictable campaigns (EU), run a 30m priming 60m before.
- Hedged multiplier: default 1.1x regional baseline; bump to 1.2x if model quantization changes are in flight or if recent preemption > 5% in 1h window.
- Failure fallback: if APAC preemption spikes and burst pool < 60% available, route 30% of noninteractive requests to EU opportunistic bucket, and inform product via status page.

Standup log snippet (afternoon check-in)
- 14:00 PT: SFO priming smoke looked good — median cold-start reduced from 420ms to 320ms in the canary pool.
- 15:10 PT: APAC spot churn observed on one provider; Diego kicked opportunistic backfill (region: EU-West) for noncritical jobs.
- 16:25 PT: Observability alerts configured — three dashboards: priming-health, slot-utilization, preemption-signal. Jon will share dashboard links in slack.

Data / quick notes from the run (numbers are approximate, captured from canary telemetry)
- Canary model: rdl-7b-quant-shared, sequence baseline 64 tokens.
- Priming effect (canary SFO): p50 latency -12%, p95 -9%, p99 -6%; warm cache hit rate jumped from 13% to 58% during the first 15m after priming.
- Cost implication: estimated incremental reserved-hours to support the hedged multiplier for APAC = +6% on reserved pool, estimated incremental spot/backfill usage -14% token cost for same throughput.

Annotated playbook (for oncall and ops rotation)
1) Pre-surge (T-minus): 90–60m out — verify model pins, enable priming flag in serving runtime canary, run synthetic probe (10% load), confirm cache warmup metrics. Owner: Marta.
2) Pre-surge (T-minus 30m) — run regional priming window (10m APAC / 30m EU), snapshot prewarm hit rate, publish to #gpu-ops. Owner: Aisha.
3) Surge window — monitor p50/p95/p99 and slot-utilization widget. If p95 > target for >5m, trigger hedged-scaling (increase reserve by +10%) and notify SRE. Owner: Jon.
4) Post-surge — reduce hedged buffer slowly (over 20m) to avoid oscillation, collect regression traces, and tag any model regressions. Owner: Diego.

Open questions / discussion bits to resolve in next sync
- How aggressive should we be with hedging multiplier during overlapping multi-region promos? (Aisha suggests region-by-region dynamic weighting; Diego suggested a global budget cap).
- Need to define SLO targets for priming health (suggestion: cache-hit >= 45% within 15m of priming, p95 tail within 1.25x baseline).
- Confirmation required from legal on whether opportunistic backfill with provider X requires additional contract disclosures.

Action items (owner — ETA)
- Marta: Expose priming API flag + canary rollout steps (PR + test plan). ETA: 2026-09-08.
- Jon: Create priming-health dashboard + alert thresholds and share links. ETA: 2026-09-04.
- Diego: Implement hedged multiplier toggle in slot manager (config + rollout plan). ETA: 2026-09-06.
- Aisha: Draft a short runbook snippet for the oncall handbook (prep/trigger/fallback). ETA: 2026-09-05.
- Samira: Coordinate deploy freeze windows and confirm no conflicting releases. ETA: 2026-09-03.

Notes to self / ideas for follow-up experiments
- Try fractional priming cadence (e.g., 3x 3m priming pulses vs 1x 10m) to reduce incremental reserved-hours while preserving cache coverage.
- Evaluate priming warm pool placement heuristic: closer to ingress vs closer to model shard. Measure network egress/latency tradeoff.
- Small A/B: optimistic hedging (1.15x) vs conservative (1.05x) and measure SLA slippage and cost delta over two campaign windows.

Appendix (useful links)
- Capacity playbook (confluence): CONFLUENCE-Infra/Capacity-Playbook
- Related jira: JIRA-INF-1842 (slot-manager toggles), JIRA-INF-1877 (priming API), JIRA-INF-1856 (apac-hedge)
